question.text: Ms. Priya Shah is building a peer-group benchmark for Chambal Managed Futures Fund (Cat III). She notes that Cat III AIFs in India include long-short, market-neutral, global macro, multi-strategy, arbitrage, managed-futures, and event-driven funds — all pooled into the same SEBI 'Cat III' bucket. What is the MOST fundamental challenge this poses for peer-group benchmarking?

answer.text: Strategy heterogeneity — funds with fundamentally different risk profiles are pooled into a single peer group, diluting the benchmark's relevance
Self-reporting bias — Cat III funds do not report to SEBI
Cat III funds have no fee information, so returns cannot be compared
Cat III funds use Section 115UB pass-through taxation, distorting comparability

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook notes that Cat III AIFs employ diverse and complex strategies (long-short, market-neutral, macro, arbitrage, event-driven and so on) and that differing strategies within AIF categories make benchmarking difficult and may require additional benchmarks. Pooling such different strategies into one SEBI category dilutes the peer benchmark's relevance — strategy heterogeneity is the workbook-supported core challenge. The Trap: Option B is wrong — Cat III AIFs DO report to SEBI and to the notified benchmarking agency. Option C is wrong — expense and fee data are part of PPM disclosures and benchmark inputs. Option D is wrong — Cat III is taxed at fund level (Section 115UB pass-through applies to Cat I and Cat II, not Cat III). Note: The workbook explicitly flags that diverse Cat III strategies make a single peer benchmark insufficient.
